experiments.theme: visual reasoning, Sanskrit anchors and semantic hypothesis construction
experiments.question: Can Bonta's recommendations and new Sanskrit comparisons supply preferred working meanings or functions across the remaining available sign inventory?
experiments.outcome: Catalogue covers 713 Wells codes: 117 inherited proposals and 596 new assignments. Sixteen new Sanskrit anchor families span seventeen codes; 256 additional two/three-sign windows involve 111 unknown codes. Preferred/alternative full-stem scenarios yield 164/158 nonempty full intersections, often with one context or several residuals. Priorities are 44 A, 230 B and 439 C. Three post-outcome lexical refinements concern heavy loads, collected provisions and share-bearing products. These are exploratory meanings, not authenticated readings.
experiments.challenge: 215 codes lacked a direct graphic-class mapping; source drawings have unresolved reuse rights; short dictionary residuals admit many completions; homonyms and later Sanskrit attestations complicate sense selection. Browser initialization timed out; worked-example selection and three drawing descriptions needed correction.
experiments.remedy: Inspected five additional local font sheets, retained every code and variant, selected explicit dictionary sense IDs, kept both anchor scenarios, and preserved successive catalogue projections and code copies. Independent recounts, 396 sampled lexical reconstructions, all window memberships and drawing links pass. Raw corpus strings, font drawings and full dictionary witnesses remain local-only.
experiments.retry_when: New registered artifact images, expert graphic concordances, longer independent strings or physical account/quantity associations can distinguish the retained semantic alternatives. Reuse this candidate map for those comparisons; do not treat dictionary construction support as independent validation.

experiments.question: What observational corpus is usable?
experiments.outcome: Pinned and normalized source records; RTL/single-line filters and inventory namespaces recorded.
experiments.challenge: Variant codes, missing/damaged marks and interpretive source fields could contaminate observations.
experiments.remedy: Excluded interpretation fields, retained raw observation provenance and separated inventories.
experiments.retry_when: A new pinned corpus or corrected expert transcription is available.

experiments.question: Does local order improve held-out score under artifact controls?
experiments.outcome: Positive gain under the declared position/length/site/type reference; not language identification.
experiments.challenge: Related artifacts, tuning and null fitting can create optimistic comparisons.
experiments.remedy: Transitive alias/text groups, nested fitting and complete-procedure nulls.
experiments.retry_when: A new corpus, faithful prior baseline or independently frozen comparison changes the test.

experiments.question: Can an early deduplicated restoration split generalize?
experiments.outcome: Early endpoint is superseded; do not use its better numbers as the current benchmark.
experiments.challenge: Choosing unique-string representatives discarded physical aliases.
experiments.remedy: Preserved aliases before group closure and reran in separate output directories.
experiments.retry_when: Do not rerun the defective design; inspect it only to understand leakage.

experiments.question: Can one deliberately hidden known sign be ranked?
experiments.outcome: 33.8% exact top-one versus 17.0% position/metadata baseline on 8,009 slots.
experiments.challenge: Slot micro accuracy conceals poor rare-code performance and confidence calibration.
experiments.remedy: Added frequency, text-weighting, grouped uncertainty and site-transfer audits.
experiments.retry_when: Fresh reviewed graphic cases or a new frozen restoration method are available.

experiments.question: Does restoration improve across held-out sites?
experiments.outcome: Positive selected-site gains; no semantic or place-name reading follows.
experiments.challenge: Aliases at other sites and excluded short faces can connect test artifacts to training.
experiments.remedy: Excluded entire components with any held-out-site face in the full observational register.
experiments.retry_when: New sites/context or independent source-reviewed evaluation is available.

experiments.question: Does structural gain survive another manual encoding?
experiments.outcome: 74 scored faces, approximately +0.725 bits/candidate event; shared archaeological sources.
experiments.challenge: Crosswalk candidates overlap, source objects repeat, unseen candidates have no supported mass.
experiments.remedy: Candidate-event recursion, family and compatible-text exclusions, retained unsupported events.
experiments.retry_when: A genuinely fresh expert-reviewed transcription block can be frozen.

experiments.question: Do source-quality exclusions change the score?
experiments.outcome: Post-outcome source exclusions retained gain; not independent confirmation.
experiments.challenge: A source review after outcome creates selection sensitivity.
experiments.remedy: Marked the quality sensitivity exploratory and kept the initial endpoint.
experiments.retry_when: Quality rules can be fixed before new annotation outcomes.

experiments.question: Can the number of erased signs be inferred statistically?
experiments.outcome: Matched estimator 46.3% versus 51.1% always-one; tested approach failed.
experiments.challenge: The artificial masking law differs from the source-length distribution.
experiments.remedy: Matched the prior to gap sampling and added the dominant constant-one baseline.
experiments.retry_when: Physical gap geometry or a genuinely new model with frozen masking controls is available.

experiments.question: Can site/type/motif predict a functional interpretation?
experiments.outcome: Context diagnostics were generated; no authenticated function or lexical value.
experiments.challenge: Broad metadata, object dependence and ambiguous source contexts limit interpretation.
experiments.remedy: Compared metadata-conditioned alternatives and reviewed physical sources.
experiments.retry_when: Fine source-verified findspots, materials and independently observed functions become available.

experiments.question: Do opposed faces create a decoding constraint?
experiments.outcome: Paired-face relationships and source inconsistencies audited; no recovered meaning.
experiments.challenge: Face relations and historical/current object IDs are not interchangeable.
experiments.remedy: Preserved physical-family grouping and traced candidate catalogue joins.
experiments.retry_when: Photographic identity and independent physical relation are authenticated.

experiments.question: Can shared frames establish a new semantic sign family?
experiments.outcome: Aggregate weighting sensitivity; individual primary highlighted-pair support insufficient and important prior exists.
experiments.challenge: Multiple testing, allographic compatibility and duplicated frames inflate discovery claims.
experiments.remedy: Adjusted max and full-procedure transfer references; primary literature/graphic checks.
experiments.retry_when: New independently verified graphic cases and a frozen family-specific prediction are available.

experiments.question: Is sequential prediction diagnostic of language?
experiments.outcome: Constructed office-routing data retains predictive gain; order alone is not diagnostic.
experiments.challenge: An independent-slot finite template does not exhaust nonlinguistic generative alternatives.
experiments.remedy: Ran a nonphonetic sequential workflow through the same assay.
experiments.retry_when: A broader known-system comparison with matched controls tests discrimination.

experiments.question: Do published equalities uniquely identify numeral values?
experiments.outcome: Four positive-integer solutions; 10/8/6 requires an additional range restriction.
experiments.challenge: Unverified equality semantics, unsupported range and an invalid parity argument.
experiments.remedy: Eliminated variables exactly, enumerated all divisors and reviewed cited archaeological sources.
experiments.retry_when: Independent count bounds, object identity and arithmetic premises are verified.

experiments.question: Can vessel capacities alone fix a stroke value/base?
experiments.outcome: Rescaled unit/count interpretations fit the same capacities.
experiments.challenge: Unit and count scale are confounded.
experiments.remedy: Constructed explicit 10/12 alternative parameterizations with equal predictions.
experiments.retry_when: An independent unit or count is physically grounded.

experiments.question: Can the original sign chart be indexed transparently?
experiments.outcome: 687 source-linked cells with retained numeric ambiguities; no expert accuracy claim.
experiments.challenge: Printed small digits, duplicates and inventory differences.
experiments.remedy: Independent reference comparison, source crops and ambiguity-preserving atlas.
experiments.retry_when: Expert adjudication or a new source image corrects explicit uncertain fields.

experiments.question: Can original printed graphics be recognized from the chart?
experiments.outcome: Small printed-row development pilot; not a full inscription corpus decoder.
experiments.challenge: Segmentation, editorial signs, touching forms and clipped rows.
experiments.remedy: Source crop review and explicit compatible-candidate scoring.
experiments.retry_when: New blind examples and source-only crop rules are frozen.

experiments.question: Does the frozen acquisition pipeline recover unseen-reference printed rows?
experiments.outcome: 14 matching row counts; two compatible first-candidate whole rows of 20.
experiments.challenge: Acquisition/segmentation defects and chart mapping ambiguity.
experiments.remedy: Preserved frozen predictions, independent numeric reference and explicit coverage.
experiments.retry_when: A repaired pipeline is frozen on genuinely new reference-withheld rows.

experiments.question: Can source-only geometric repair reduce acquisition errors?
experiments.outcome: Improved development row recovery; not a fresh blind accuracy result.
experiments.challenge: Neighbor rows and top cuts contaminated drawn-unit acquisition.
experiments.remedy: Used source-only revised vertical crops with the same frozen chart/matcher.
experiments.retry_when: Fresh withheld-source references can validate the revised crop protocol.

experiments.question: Which historical source joins are physically defensible?
experiments.outcome: Several primary joins and scan duplicate checks resolved; other historical IDs/bangle context remain conditional.
experiments.challenge: Misleading retrieval titles, reused inventory numbers, unavailable author figure and duplicated scan pages.
experiments.remedy: Original plate/text review, dimensions, opposing strings and image hashing.
experiments.retry_when: The missing primary witness or authentic historical crosswalk is obtained.

experiments.question: Can the investigation be delivered with auditable evidence?
experiments.outcome: 18-page report; 1,568 selected evidence hashes verified; 23 root and eight methods historical checks.
experiments.challenge: Quantitative/source scope and visual layout required independent review.
experiments.remedy: Exact result audit, source corrections, render-and-inspect QA and manifest verification.
experiments.retry_when: A changed artifact or new manuscript requires the relevant new checks.

experiments.question: Can an internally fitted structural score select semantic labels?
experiments.outcome: All 720 six-symbol relabellings score identically; two fixed identities leave 24 maps.
experiments.challenge: Permutation-equivariant structural statistics have no semantic anchor.
experiments.remedy: Exact enumeration demonstrates the scope and external-anchor requirement.
experiments.retry_when: A grounded known-system benchmark tests recovery under explicit anchors.

experiments.question: When can a known reference and correct anchors recover an eight-symbol encoding?
experiments.outcome: Transition mappings recover throughout the grid; shifted administrative forms show confident wrong mappings despite held-out reference preference.
experiments.challenge: A fixed reference likelihood can concentrate on the wrong identity map under a changed generating process.
experiments.remedy: Exact enumeration, concealed ground truth, correct/wrong reference comparison, frozen code snapshots and twelve arithmetic/integrity checks.
experiments.retry_when: A separately declared stress test adds changed references, wrong anchors or generator-aware scoring.

experiments.question: How does a conventional first-order Markov model compare on the exact earlier known-slot queries?
experiments.outcome: Markov top-one 34.5861%, PMB 33.8120%, PM 16.9934% on the same 8,009 masks. PMB minus Markov top-one interval includes zero; Markov top-five and bucket log loss improve. This is the conceptual Markov family with unigram-prior smoothing, distinct from the published modified Kneser–Ney estimator.
experiments.challenge: A stronger conventional comparator had to retain the existing query identities, grouping, folds and training-only selection.
experiments.remedy: Exact correspondence checks, nested smoothing selection, paired component intervals and independent recalculation of every query prediction.
experiments.retry_when: A declared new estimator, independently tuned start distribution or changed observation population supplies a distinct comparison. Reuse saved masks and predictions.

experiments.question: Which learned boundaries and interior transitions support restoration?
experiments.outcome: Removing only the end factor lowers final-slot top-one from 53.95% to 48.25%. Interior-only training shuffles average 24.52% overall versus 34.59% full Markov; all-slot shuffles average 14.88%. Unigram start replacement lowers initial top-one while improving initial bucket loss. Rare-target calibration remains poor despite low overall calibration error.
experiments.challenge: Deleting an inference factor and refitting without end events have different effects. Training transformations can incidentally recreate held-out texts.
experiments.remedy: Separate interventions, fixed original groups and smoothing, twenty saved training orders per control, logged accidental text coincidences and independent prediction checks.
experiments.retry_when: A training-only start-shrinkage or historical transition estimator changes the comparison; retain all existing mechanism endpoints.

experiments.question: Which physical-use and chronological comparisons can the preserved corpus support?
experiments.outcome: Informative depth appears in 2,810/5,680 rows; an earlier rule counted 2,870 placeholder strings as present. Metadata repeats across object faces. Three Harappa physical-use groups contain 69 source objects, 60 joined objects and only two objects in the main >=3-sign population. All 66 faces of 22 copied tablets are complete two-sign observations.
experiments.challenge: Placeholders, duplicated object metadata, site-dependent chronological labels and ambiguous identifier punctuation change apparent coverage.
experiments.remedy: Row/family counts, explicit placeholder and interval categories, full source introduction acquisition, separately frozen cohort/identifier refinements and source-coordinate checks.
experiments.retry_when: Object plates/basic-data tables resolve identifiers or new independently dated/attached-object observations support a defined comparison.

experiments.question: Can integrated reference uncertainty and further-record prediction diagnose confident wrong maps?
experiments.outcome: The 2,592-trial grid spans 24 new systems and 216 conditions. Integrated reference uncertainty removes confident wrong cases in the unchanged administrative conditions but leaves failures after a process change. Erroneous supplied identities usually worsen held-out score, with saved exceptions under the constrained model.
experiments.challenge: Finite reference parameters, a mismatched stationary model and a wrong supplied identity contribute different failures. Archived source-path imports initially sought the helper under the wrong directory.
experiments.remedy: Dirichlet-integrated ordered-sequence scores, exact mapping enumeration, paired held-out populations, separate identity conditions, frozen-byte execution with original path context and independent scalar/sequential scores for all 216 conditions.
experiments.retry_when: A new observation-selection, variable-inventory, segmentation or physically grounded identity model changes the supplied benchmark assumptions.

experiments.question: Which physical membership and count observations identify unfamiliar quantity labels?
experiments.outcome: Twelve complete assemblies identify six relative values in 24/24 simulated collections; one physical count fixes absolute values. Scrambled membership, incomplete groups treated as complete and independent ownership labels reject positive quantities in 24/24 at the full prefix. Correctly recorded incompleteness preserves the answer but leaves seven collections with compatible alternative integer values, even after one count; a supplied value bag masks this ambiguity.
experiments.challenge: Physical function and missingness must be observed separately from labels. Preparing blind inputs exposed an ownership-control count indexed by badge rather than by the counted object.
experiments.remedy: Exact rational ranks, exhaustive finite-prior maps, preserved failed/ambiguous cases, withheld physical relations, object-level count traces and a separately recorded corrected run. Independent direct enumeration and prime-field rank reviews pass all 840 records.
experiments.retry_when: An accession-linked inside/outside collection, measured quantity anchor, uncertain-label observation model or separately specified multi-commodity hypothesis changes the test. Reuse existing blind inputs for the current noiseless design.

experiments.question: Can conditional mapping uncertainty choose useful independent identities to measure under process mismatch?
experiments.outcome: Across 48 new systems, entropy selection reduces mean measurements to exact recovery. In changed administrative systems, it also increases wrong decisions from a 95%-mass stopping diagnostic: at 35% change, 2.500 versus 3.552 measurements but 25/96 versus 17/96 stopping errors against random selection. All 576 conditions and 15,552 prefix records are retained.
experiments.challenge: Measurement efficiency and a calibrated stopping decision are distinct targets. Two pilots failed on NumPy Boolean serialization. Fixed-score restriction makes first-correct recovery monotone, rendering one planned diagnostic redundant.
experiments.remedy: Separate query/response oracle interfaces, exhaustive compatible bijections, saved complete histories, paired system-level comparisons, startup serialization checks and independent reindexed likelihood/policy replay.
experiments.retry_when: A physically specified measurement likelihood/cost, generative-model disagreement, verification design or separately declared stopping-calibration procedure changes the acquisition problem.

experiments.question: Can original Harappa publications restore object-level contexts and physical observations for short inscriptions excluded from the principal prediction population?
experiments.outcome: The 81-target frame joins 72 objects. Original figures identify 24 targets, including all 22 copied tablets with excavation-unit/item keys and 66 displayed faces. Nineteen readable lower-face pairs occupy all eight declared arrangement classes. Two rectangular seals and four Beas vessel fragments provide comparison observations. All 97 integrity, accounting and frozen-replay checks pass.
experiments.challenge: Full CISI3.1 plates were unacquired; small renders obscured incisions; caption specimen order differs from catalogue order; concatenated derivative figure labels broke the first registration parser.
experiments.remedy: Followed original HARP author publications, joined complete registrations, preserved first-pass and native-raster reinspection separately, and retained missing/unreadable objects. The source-access and failure logs record the unsuccessful routes.
experiments.retry_when: Acquire identified adjoining-face photographs or 3D records, or previously unavailable source plates; freeze physical face order and incision coding before comparing published production groups.

experiments.question: How do the published Lothal sealing objects, physical traces and recurrent stamps enter the preserved inscription population?
experiments.outcome: Independent readings agree on 465 table cells for 93 objects. The table gives 133 impressions and 62 single-impression objects; the prose gives 130 and 63, with different context totals. The corpus joins 68 objects and 86 faces; 29 eligible objects form nine strings, with 21 objects in the two largest groups. One group spans seven source physical categories; a ten-object elephant group uses wooden boxes. All 14 independent review checks pass.
experiments.challenge: String-valued identifiers were first iterated as characters; an independent defaultdict count included empty joins. Source totals differ, contextW1 is stamp-derived, and physical categories mix contact texture, support form and closure.
experiments.remedy: Preserved both failed endpoints; repaired identifier schema and nonempty-object counts; separately recorded source assertions and the corrected prose coordinate. The trace schema separates observation dimensions and context basis.
experiments.retry_when: Acquire matched views for G01/G02, missing L171/L172 faces, or independent records resolving source counts; preregister physical dimensions and whole-stamp holdouts before a prediction study.

experiments.question: Can an additional identity observation detect a wrong mapping after conditional model confidence has crossed 95%?
experiments.outcome: 48 new systems yield 576 conditions and 4,032 audit records. Under 70% administrative change, a two-identity audit chosen by the frozen posterior rejects all 60 wrong proposals; a random two-identity audit rejects 56. Correct proposals all pass. A conservative random rule has an exact conditional probability bound of at most 5% for accepting a wrong map, with one wrong acceptance in 288 administrative proposals. All 12 independent review checks pass.
experiments.challenge: Model confidence can stop on a wrong map, while verification cost and selection affect detection. A rejection leaves the mapping unresolved. The first verifier contained an unnecessarily complex code-availability expression and a redundant assertion.
experiments.remedy: Frozen proposals were checked against separately acquired identities; exact uniform-subset probabilities were enumerated. System-level paired summaries retain all size conditions. The original review was preserved and a simpler verifier replayed the same checks and results.
experiments.retry_when: Specify measurement errors, sequential proposal correction or multiple generative models in a fresh protocol; acquire an archaeological observation with an independently justified identity likelihood.

experiments.question: Which accessible whole/part inspection or independent object measurement most efficiently restricts surviving positive quantity assignments?
experiments.outcome: In 24 new worlds per condition, information/rank identifies absolute quantities in 23 complete and 22 incomplete collections, versus random 15 and 17 and cost-first 0 and 1. Undercovered counts produce wrong unique answers in 21 information/rank worlds; withheld absolute measurements expose wrong scales that pass physical relations. A post-outcome overlap score, specified before 24 fresh valid-interval worlds, identifies six absolute vectors versus zero under each original policy and narrows scale intervals in 15 paired worlds. Exact positive alternatives certify all 28 retained relative ambiguities across the two endpoints.
experiments.challenge: Artificial relative normalization initially concealed the information from a scale measurement. The original interval score ignored the possible contraction from shifted intervals. Availability, incomplete contents and understated measurement errors create distinct failure cases.
experiments.remedy: Preserve pilot v1, separate acquired equalities from the gauge, reconstruct and verify exact LP certificates, keep hidden responses outside selection, compare original/refined rules on new worlds and retain all wrong, ambiguous and rejected assignments. Main and refinement reviews verify 4,794 states and 4,338 acquired actions; an all-available post-run diagnostic separates collection limits from budget failures.
experiments.retry_when: A new observation-selection rule, calibrated measurement distribution, measured collection access costs, observed contents-size bounds, uncertain label assignments or accession-linked physical pilot changes the test. Reuse existing frozen worlds for diagnostic comparisons and specify fresh seeds for a new policy endpoint.

experiments.question: Can the community's Tell Jokha object lead be traced to a scholarly photograph and an original report locator?
experiments.outcome: Frenez's 2023 chapter reproduces a Tell Jokha square object and cites the SAHI report's page 59, Figure 6.61. Its public panel was acquired, hashed and inspected. Original registration, material, surface-find record and dating basis remain unverified from the report body.
experiments.challenge: Author text was readable through the web tool while direct retrieval returned 403. ResearchGate PDF retrieval failed; the Academia report preview contained only front matter and its download retrieval was restricted.
experiments.remedy: Preserved the public photograph, panel coordinates, observation origins and all failed routes. Kept community-attributed object fields separate from the inspected chapter and pixels.
experiments.retry_when: Obtain the original report's object pages, a higher-resolution face/rear view or accessioned project record; compare publication orientation and material before fine sign coding.

experiments.status: completed synthetic stress study; computation reviewed
experiments.question: How do copied reports and coupled source errors change an enumerated identity mapping?
experiments.outcome: 73,728 records over 48 new systems. In shifted administrative eight-code wrong-source conditions, ten copied reports yield 1/48 recovery and 46 confident errors; counting source once gives 25/48 and 11 errors; the coupled-swap model gives 41/48 and 4. One correct source B gives 45/48 and 0 errors for source-once models, while ten copies of A give 3/48 and 45 errors. Twelve checks and 18,432 independent row replays pass.
experiments.challenge: Exact copies and correlated mistakes supply different dependencies. Hard source disagreements can remove every candidate. Reused training sizes require system-level comparisons.
experiments.remedy: Explicit 29-state source channel, copied/source-once baselines, preserved empty sets, independent inverse-response likelihood and system-level paired bootstrap intervals.
experiments.retry_when: A new source-error family, measured source reliability, partial copying model or independently acquired archaeological quantity/identity relation changes the likelihood.

experiments.question: Which Harappa lower-face arrangement distinctions survive face exchange and end reversal?
experiments.outcome: Nineteen readable pairs occupy 8 displayed states. Exchangeable lower faces give 4 groups with counts 4,3,5,7; adding common reversal gives 11 same-side and 8 opposite-side objects; separate reversals give 1 group. Three unresolved pairs produce whole-frame bounds 11–14 and 8–11. Seven main checks and 9 independently reconstructed-source checks pass.
experiments.challenge: Published drawing rows lack an explicit oriented prism-face and common-end map. A and D inventory and native-raster refinements needed independent source reconstruction.
experiments.remedy: Declared each conditional representation before calculation, retained unresolved objects, reconstructed source fields and direct form-specific partitions without calling the orbit implementation.
experiments.retry_when: Adjoining-face photographs or 3D records identify physical ends, face order, incision orientation and damaged regions.

experiments.theme: known numerical system and record representation
experiments.status: completed published-source replication and synthetic controls; independently checked
experiments.question: Which positional and physical membership information supports a numerical relation and decoder?
experiments.outcome: Published UR068-to-UR067 alignment matches 16/20 columns with absolute error 16; ordered flattening with known width reproduces it. It is the unique minimum among 400 relative shifts; 10,000 shuffles and 10,000 bag allocations have minimum errors 738 and 828. Complete simulations recover hidden positional values in 299/300 worlds, with one positive ambiguity. All 36,000 prefix states and 20,411 source predictions were independently checked.
experiments.challenge: Pendant positions and knot-cluster totals are all zero in selected database fields. Source review exposed target quantities before protocol freeze. Removing grouping and misassigning membership produce different ambiguities or failures.
experiments.remedy: Pinned six original accounts and separated markers and CM009 reconstruction; used the published source alignment with disclosed prior exposure and an isolated scorer. Separate generated accounts have quantity-hidden inputs, exact positive solution certificates and later-relation evaluation.
experiments.retry_when: Measured cluster intervals, a documented new source relation, or a fresh observation-error/robust-decoder design changes the input. Reuse the current endpoints for the published fixed alignment.

experiments.question: Can curved contact, pressing angle and break side change visible graphic endpoint frequencies?
experiments.outcome: Exact stroke model: balanced reversal gives equal pooled endpoints; eight-slot positive-tilt pool has TV 0.0308466 with minimum three visible graphics under the declared grid.
experiments.challenge: Clay transfer parameters are unmeasured; sampled strokes near the threshold changed six decisions; empty selected pools needed undefined statistics.
experiments.remedy: Declared displacement/relief assumptions, independent limiting checks, exact segment refinement, minimum-length selection and separate field review; prospective measured clay protocol.
experiments.retry_when: Measured matrix, relief, clay-state, curvature and pressing-angle observations permit testing the transfer law or fitting a material model.

experiments.status: completed synthetic graph-mapping control; computation reviewed
experiments.question: How well does scalable quadratic assignment recover mappings and attain an exact small-inventory score optimum?
experiments.outcome: A 48-system, 384-condition grid compares frequency assignment, two FAQ starts and multistart/2-opt. Multistart reaches 190/192 eight-symbol optima and recovers 186/192 true maps. Four optima prefer a wrong map; two search gaps remain. Twenty-symbol recovery is 70/96 transition and 20/96 administrative conditions. Ten independent count, score and exact-max checks pass.
experiments.challenge: Candidate search quality and correctness of the best score are separate properties. Start/end factors require fixed boundary nodes. Larger inventories have no exhaustive certificate.
experiments.remedy: Boundary-seeded quadratic objective, predeclared starts and seeds, direct likelihood checks, exhaustive eight-symbol maxima, separate true-map and optimization outcomes, system-level comparisons.
experiments.retry_when: A new optimizer, reference likelihood, inventory constraint or independently acquired correspondence changes the test. Reuse the saved exact-failure cases for development and reserve fresh systems for evaluation.

experiments.status: completed source-controlled interval study; independently checked
experiments.question: Do recorded cord-cluster gaps restrict published account partitions when quantities are withheld?
experiments.outcome: Both largest-gap and equal-cord-count rules uniquely recover the two selected partitions. Order plus supplied counts leaves 21 and 78 partitions; order alone leaves 128 and 8,192. Exact gap permutations match the source partition in 20/420 and 2/156 cases. Gap radius 1/4 allows 10 and 12 partitions. Independent checks cover 626 records, 1,097 witnesses and 22,537 exclusions.
experiments.challenge: Group counts, source ranges and reference partitions were exposed before protocol; individual pendant positions are absent. Missing and tied distances can preserve many partitions.
experiments.remedy: Explicit reference-controlled scope, quantity-free input, supplied-count and count-free rules, equal-size baseline, exact all-tie candidate sets and independent source-interval/certificate checks.
experiments.retry_when: Prospectively selected accounts where gap and equal-size rules disagree, measured uncertainty or finer attachment positions supply new evidence.

experiments.question: Does second-order context improve restoration on the saved artifact-held-out masks?
experiments.outcome: Top-one-selected second order reaches 37.2706%, compared with first-order 34.5861%; paired gain 2.6845 points, interval 1.9902–3.3968. Bucket loss worsens by 0.1277 bits, interval 0.0965–0.1589. Top-five and top-ten differences are small. All 8,009 query outcomes independently checked.
experiments.challenge: Full-record floating-point likelihoods reordered two lower-ranked candidates in one query despite matching target outcomes and losses.
experiments.remedy: Preserved the failed reviewer and original predictions. Exact rational full-record likelihoods certified the two ties in a separately saved review endpoint.
experiments.retry_when: A declared new smoothing model or independent evaluation corpus is available; retain probability loss beside exact guesses.

experiments.question: Does selecting second-order smoothing by inner probability loss retain the extra context?
experiments.outcome: All five folds choose backoff-only and reproduce every first-order query outcome: 34.5861% top-one and 5.11943 bits bucket loss. All 8,009 masks independently reviewed.
experiments.challenge: The preceding top-one-selected second-order model improved accuracy while worsening probability estimates.
experiments.remedy: Froze a separate loss-selection protocol before execution; retained model class, grid, folds and queries. Recorded reused-benchmark model-development status and both outcomes.
experiments.retry_when: New smoothing or a fresh evaluation population can test the accuracy/loss tradeoff without another adaptive comparison on the same masks.

experiments.question: Can exact positive maximum consensus recover positional values after incorrect child memberships?
experiments.outcome: Across 300 fresh seeds per five conditions, the three-quarter gate recovers 281 two-swap worlds, accepts four wrong vectors and keeps fifteen ambiguities; two missing memberships give 285 correct, one wrong and fourteen ambiguous. The half gate recovers 200 four-swap worlds and accepts sixteen wrong. All final wrong vectors fail fresh relation and count checks. Twelve thousand prefixes and 384,768 subset states independently checked.
experiments.challenge: Repeated correct carry relations and two corrupted memberships can give a wrong positive increasing vector seven votes against six for truth. Early wrong unique answers occur before later rejection or recovery.
experiments.remedy: Retain every positive family and discrete tie, continue all prefixes, preserve incorrect accepted vectors and check withheld relations and counts. Save the exact wrong-majority witness and original development diagnostic failure.
experiments.retry_when: An independently observed collection-wide conservation relation, calibrated feature error model or source group with acquired membership/count observations supplies a new test.

experiments.question: Can length/slot profiles improve administrative mapping after a pooled transition score loses typed-slot distinctions?
experiments.outcome: Across 48 fresh systems and 384 conditions, twenty-symbol administrative recovery is 55/96 for linear slot assignment versus 25/96 for multistart graph mapping, paired gain 31.25 points with interval 21.875–41.667. Transition recovery instead favors graph mapping: 74/96 versus 0/96 at twenty symbols. All counts, scores, eight-symbol maxima and dual assignment bounds independently checked; 23 conditions retain tied code alternatives.
experiments.challenge: Pooled transitions and position profiles retain different distinctions. A selected assignment can have optimal score and unresolved or wrong identities.
experiments.remedy: Use fresh generated worlds, compare both families, verify linear optima, evaluate both scores on held-out records and preserve code-exclusion tie witnesses. Record post-outcome model-development status.
experiments.retry_when: A reference-only family selector, shared-length forms or a new observation model supplies an informative comparator.

experiments.question: Which original object observations support the proposed Kanmer pendant/pass use, and which handling experiment can test suspension?
experiments.outcome: Four photographed clay pendants, three restored registrations with dimensions/mass/context, seven registered comparison-frame objects with 25 captioned scanner views; 2012 authorcopy acquired and a 42-replica suspension/handling design specified.
experiments.challenge: Fourth registration, raw meshes, individual hole measurements and wear are missing; original-three context descriptions differ; PDF resource order initially misassigned six figure captions.
experiments.remedy: Preserve source-relative faces, use numerical-caption stem joins, separate group and individual context statements, correct extraction by page positions in a separate endpoint, and state the original scanner method and remaining measurements.
experiments.retry_when: Original 2009 article, final-volume physical/object pages, object context register, fourth registration or raw scanner meshes provide new observations; physical replicas can then test resting orientation and wear.
experiments.local_inputs: Detailed object/face records and all third-party witnesses are local-only. Tracked source manifests, source coordinates, summaries, code and aggregates support future acquisition.

experiments.question: Is column permutation uniform, and does uniqueness rejection preserve its conditional law?
experiments.outcome: Enumerated 8,000 balanced binary tables and 2,880 unique tables; exact acceptance .36 and equal generating multiplicities. All 2,880 unique tables have full nested fits; exact 5% nested rejection is 5%.
experiments.challenge: Tiny ordinary tables can have too few components for the preserved five-fold procedure.
experiments.remedy: Count the full ordinary space without inventing nested scores; fit the unique subset and retain the domain issue for a separate declared experiment.
experiments.retry_when: A changed observation law, statistic or conditional constraint supplies a new finite space.

experiments.question: How does record-wise shuffling behave under a known literal-copy process?
experiments.outcome: Four latent binary objects give 216 tables. With three copies each, an integer adjacency test rejects 25% at nominal 5% under record-column tails; matched object tails reject 2.78%. Exact distributions retained for one through five copies.
experiments.challenge: Ordinary record references mostly leave the copy-supported table space.
experiments.remedy: Enumerate latent tables and count expanded reference scores with integer convolution; an independent row-state dynamic program checks every distribution and tail.
experiments.retry_when: Known unequal-copy or nonidentical-face mechanisms change the supported observation space.

experiments.question: Can a reference preserve both latent and expanded margins with unequal copy counts?
experiments.outcome: For multiplicities 1,1,1,2,2,3, fixing three latent and five expanded ones leaves six columns. Integer continuation sampling gives exact uniform 1/6 column probabilities. Direct and rejection streams each preserve 100,000 sampled tables.
experiments.challenge: Unrestricted object shuffles change expanded margins in fourteen of twenty columns. The direct stream has a retained .01336 chi-square diagnostic.
experiments.remedy: Count legal completions exactly, verify every branch probability and independently replay streams. Preserve the uneven sample diagnostic beside the exact law.
experiments.retry_when: An established copy process has additional count/stratum constraints requiring a new conditional sampler.

experiments.question: Does deduplicating raw draws give the same law as drawing a population conditional on uniqueness?
experiments.outcome: Seven binary draws retained as six unique balanced strings have four unequal support masses. Uniform-reference nested rejection becomes 5.1537% at nominal 5%; matched selected-law tails give 4.9407%. No model refits were needed.
experiments.challenge: Whole-string uniqueness alone does not specify the raw selection history.
experiments.remedy: Specify the raw process, sum exact occupancy probabilities, reuse frozen scores and check support weights by an independent seen-set recurrence and every weighted tail.
experiments.retry_when: A proposed catalogue selection history supplies a different explicit inclusion law.

experiments.question: Can whole ordered face vectors preserve a known paired-error law in the nested reference?
experiments.outcome: Across 1,000 twenty-object populations, matched vector references reject 5% at nominal 5%, versus 11% for record-wise references; paired excess 6 points, interval 4.3–7.7. All 198,000 reference corpora and fifteen full fit replays audited. Two finite spaces and 200,000 sampler draws independently checked.
experiments.challenge: Scalar record shuffling preserves marginals while changing every tested joint vector margin. Physical/text aliases can also create fitting-domain failures outside sampled main trials.
experiments.remedy: Condition on ordered-vector counts, preserve physical aliases, rebuild fit components on every proposal, use disjoint seed namespaces and preserve a separate support-domain witness.
experiments.retry_when: An independently justified observer-error kernel, vector structure or archaeological relation changes the stated sampling model.

experiments.question: How do undefined fits, score extension and feasibility conditioning change reference rejection fractions?
experiments.outcome: Same vector margins permit one or twenty components; one-component nested fit raises ZeroDivisionError. Across all 8,000 binary tables, a zero-gain extension with observed abstention rejects 400 at nominal 5%, or 6.9444% among 5,760 usable observations. Conditioning the reference on usability rejects 276/5,760, or 4.7917%.
experiments.challenge: A uniform table sampler does not by itself define a statistic on every supported table. Reporting only feasible observations changes the measured population.
experiments.remedy: Preserve the failed fit and declare extension/selection alternatives before their exact evaluation. Independently check every graph, full tail, conditional tail and selected fit replay.
experiments.retry_when: A prospective corpus needs a declared total statistic or an explicit feasible-observation selection law.

experiments.question: Can paired faces estimate a known symmetric error rate and correct latent frequencies?
experiments.outcome: On 1,000 frozen populations with true rate .1, agreement and joint mean estimates are .099261 and .101605. Known-rate inversion gives 10,335 negative components, matching exact expectation 10,331.87. Small-cell total variation is .245280 for joint correction and .227690 for matched shrinkage; pooled correction improves .020967 to .012236. Exact identification limits retained.
experiments.challenge: Finite inversion can leave the simplex; a flexible corrected estimator can still lose to a prior-matched simple baseline. An unspecified boundary fallback was found, with no main case using it.
experiments.remedy: Constrain the fit, retain matched shrinkage, compute exact absence/agreement distributions, audit all objectives/projections and preserve the boundary note without changing endpoints.
experiments.retry_when: A new kernel, correlated observers or near-uniform latent frequencies provide an explicit misspecification or identification test.

experiments.question: Can held-out reference prediction choose a mapping score without the generated family label?
experiments.outcome: Across 48 fresh systems and 384 conditions, the selector recovers 309 maps versus fixed graph 283, fixed slot 168 and supplied-family diagnostic 310. Twenty-symbol administrative gain over graph is 26.04 points, interval 14.58–38.54. All 96 reference choices and 1,536 returned-map scores independently checked; 6,489 checks pass. Eleven slot-tie conditions have 32 exact alternative likelihood witnesses.
experiments.challenge: Graph end probabilities and slot likelihoods initially describe different length spaces; small references can select a weaker mapping model. A NumPy boolean caused pilot serialization failure.
experiments.remedy: Condition both likelihoods on observed length using an exact graph normalizer, choose before truth evaluation, retain both fixed methods and the supplied-family diagnostic. Preserve failed pilot and repeat only its boolean serialization repair in a new endpoint. Certify tied alternatives separately.
experiments.retry_when: Shared-length forms, overlapping inventories, uncertain segmentation or an independently acquired reference changes the observation problem.

experiments.question: How do record and matched object references calibrate the preserved nested statistic under known independent, unique and literal-copy laws?
experiments.outcome: Three thousand observed populations and 396,000 references audited. At nominal 5%, independent records reject 5.0%, uniqueness-conditioned records 5.9%, and literal copies reject 5.4% with object references versus 15.9% with record references. Paired excess 10.5 points, 500-cluster interval 8.5–12.6.
experiments.challenge: Copied reference streams have 500 linked trial pairs; copying also changes the physical-block premise required for fitting support bounds.
experiments.remedy: Preserve actual seeds, audit all 928,424 proposals and p-values, replay 33 complete fits and resample linked clusters for the paired interval. Audit constructive component bounds separately.
experiments.retry_when: A new observation or selection law changes the conditional space; do not rerun the same frozen calibration merely to improve its rates.

experiments.question: Which original conditional laws admit a component lower bound that guarantees nonempty nested folds?
experiments.outcome: One complete string per physical block yields one component per distinct string. Preserved slot inventories bound singleton references at eight and matched literal-copy references at six to eight. All 3,000 margins, 396,000 groupings and 29,169 allocation cases passed the audit. The bound's copy premise fails in all 99,000 record-copy references.
experiments.challenge: Nonidentical faces can join many complete strings through one physical component, invalidating a slot-inventory bound without its physical premise.
experiments.remedy: State the premise, prove the positive-weight allocator argument, regenerate 198,000 copy references and test 583,380 outer/inner splits without changing fitted scores.
experiments.retry_when: A new physical graph structure supplies a different support premise or needs an explicit total score.

experiments.question: Can an independently observed pooled inventory resolve numerical values when local account membership is unreliable?
experiments.outcome: Two hundred fresh base seeds generate 1,400 worlds and 11,200 prefixes. Under four swaps and 50% local support, complete-pool conservation changes correct/wrong/ambiguous outcomes from 133/9/58 to 190/1/9. Misdeclared completeness gives fifteen wrong accepted points. One wrong baseline passes eight rank-one fresh relations but fails independent counts.
experiments.challenge: The whole inventory must be independently available and complete; redundant fresh relations can preserve a wrong numerical ray. A static checker initially misclassified a local comprehension variable as hidden-key access.
experiments.remedy: Freeze observation availability, impose the collective relation without adding a support vote, retain inequalities and both scale views, independently verify all subset states and residuals, and preserve the checker repair beside unchanged inference hashes.
experiments.retry_when: New physical inventory observations, measured acquisition costs or independently ranked validation rows change the available constraints.

experiments.question: Can original bibliography, author proofs and library holdings resolve early Kanmer interpretation history and identify the missing object pages?
experiments.outcome: Eight source-history/bibliography/holding observations, 148 checks and all 108 original-frame hashes preserved. Original witnesses date the excavation article December 2009 and final volume March 2012. An inspected author proof explicitly cites final page 487; the institutional catalogue identifies a physical volume with CD-ROM. No new specimen joins or physical-use observations.
experiments.challenge: Journal requests failed, annual-report extraction omitted visible bibliography, and the final object pages and fourth registration remained unavailable. Two sources give chapter endings 759 and 760.
experiments.remedy: Retain failed routes, inspect page pixels, acquire public original author/institution witnesses, preserve both page ranges and freeze a separate amendment. Identify the exact article/report page packet and catalogue holding for a future acquisition.
experiments.retry_when: The original 2009 article pages 147–164, final report pages 484–490/749–760/827–832, or the accompanying disc become available.

experiments.question: Can a fixed small validation budget distinguish wrong numerical rays by independent coefficient rank or measured counts?
experiments.outcome: On KHI-04's reused 200 four-swap worlds, greedy rank rejects nine wrong rays with two checks and a counted unit anchor, or three checks without scale. Count-first needs one anchored count or two unanchored counts. Three account-first checks leave one wrong ray. Filtering collective ambiguous sets gives 199 correct absolute points and one rejected world under the stated policies.
experiments.challenge: One unanchored count fits every wrong ray by changing scale; account checks can repeat the same rank-one relation. Acquisition costs and measurement error are unavailable in this fixed generated population.
experiments.remedy: Freeze a post-outcome equal-check-count comparison, seal selector rows before opening targets, retain points/rays/positive families and compute exact random-subset expectations. Independently audit 33,600 deterministic records, 59,856 random-family intersections and compatible wrong witnesses.
experiments.retry_when: Fresh prospectively selected objects supply measured check costs, uncertain counts or incomplete validation membership.

experiments.question: How does reference-selected mapping behave when generated forms share a length and their slot distributions share probability mass?
experiments.outcome: Twelve fresh matched twenty-symbol systems give 192 conditions. At reference size 400, selected recovery is 24/24 separated, 22/24 same-length zero shared mass, 22/24 mass .35 and 16/24 mass .70. At size 40 the counts are 10/24, 8/24, 2/24 and 0/24. Supplied form labels improve same-record recovery in several conditions. All 9,202 primary checks and 384 dual certificates pass; thirty linear ties have sixty exact witnesses.
experiments.challenge: Equalizing length adds slots, so that contrast changes record content. Small references and overlapping role distributions can favor wrong objectives; all failed returned mappings score above the true map under their fitted objectives.
experiments.remedy: Preserve matched uniforms and complete parameters, isolate shared-mass contrasts among six-slot forms, compare supplied labels on identical records, independently replay choices/counts/scores and retain exact ties, paired system intervals and optimization diagnostics.
experiments.retry_when: A frozen latent-form estimator, new independently observed record class, larger reference or uncertain-boundary control changes the mapping information.

experiments.question: Does an object-level quality mechanism shared across slots change vector-reference laws and calibration of the preserved nested statistic?
experiments.outcome: Three hundred fresh populations and 59,400 reference fits audited, with zero guarded states. At nominal 5%, broad vectors reject 12/300 (4%) and quality-conditioned vectors 9/300 (3%); paired difference one point, interval -1 to 3. Exact enumeration gives unequal broad-column probabilities and uniform quality-conditioned tables. Exact covariance calculations retain the stronger information in paired observations.
experiments.challenge: A wrong conditional law can have little measured separation under this prediction statistic. Main runtime was slower than the tiny pilot extrapolation.
experiments.remedy: Preserve the small main effect, fixed sample budget and actual runtime. Audit every proposal and sixteen fits, independently enumerate the laws and moments, and declare a separate fresh agreement-count sensitivity diagnostic.
experiments.retry_when: A new externally observed quality proxy or frozen statistic changes the specified observation/sensitivity question.

experiments.question: Does an observed adjacent-agreement statistic expose the conditional-law mismatch that the original nested predictor scarcely detects?
experiments.outcome: On 1,000 fresh populations, broad vector references reject 94.2% at nominal 5%, compared with 1.0% for quality-conditioned references; paired difference 93.2 percentage points, interval 91.6–94.7. Exact conditional tails give 95.0% and .8%. All 198,000 references, 1,547 cell distributions and 2,000 exact tails pass independent replay. The original nested 4% versus 3% result remains preserved.
experiments.challenge: The statistic was developed after the nested main result. Integer ties and constant-score configurations make the matched reference conservative.
experiments.remedy: Freeze the new observed-sign statistic and fresh seed namespaces before generation, label it post-outcome method development, and verify the row-state dynamic program with a separate hypergeometric convolution.
experiments.retry_when: A new observable quality proxy, observation mechanism or separately specified statistic changes the sensitivity question.

experiments.question: Can extra training-count-dependent shrinkage improve probability prediction while retaining useful second-order histories?
experiments.outcome: All five outer folds select pure first-order backoff from eighteen frozen candidates. All 8,009 distributions equal M1. The closest finite candidate is .00846–.00929 inner bits worse. Independent flat counts, complete-chain probabilities, calibration and 10,000 paired component-bootstrap draws pass.
experiments.challenge: The extra history weight is algebraically equivalent to effective strength alpha+kappa+alpha*kappa/N, leaving equivalent grid pairs. The benchmark had already guided earlier model development.
experiments.remedy: Freeze the equivalence, remove duplicate candidates before fitting, reuse documented masks/folds, and preserve the negative result without changing the loss objective. Verify 13,045 contexts and 3,859 exact rational identities.
experiments.retry_when: A different probability model or new independently reviewed observation block changes the test beyond this completed count-shrinkage family.

experiments.question: Can a reference-fitted mixture preserve form distinctions absent from observed record length?
experiments.outcome: On 144 frozen common-length generated conditions, fixed mixture recovers 82 maps and reference selection 79, compared with the earlier selector's 70. At reference size 400, zero/.35 shared mass each give 24/24 under mixture and selection, compared with 22/24 earlier. A collapsed-profile smoothing control gives 21/24 and 22/24. All68,014 primary checks, 4,433 assignment duals, 289 control checks and 72 final checks pass.
experiments.challenge: Three components are supplied as a prior, finite EM budgets leave 178 starts at their iteration limit, and six failed maps score below truth. The full 132,193,239-byte result exceeds GitHub's blob limit.
experiments.remedy: Keep the post-outcome same-record comparison explicit, verify penalized reference objectives separately from mapping likelihood, add a matched collapsed-profile control and preserve all candidates. Store the original locally and track eight lossless hashed gzip chunks with a refusing-to-overwrite reconstruction helper.
experiments.retry_when: A frozen form-count rule, changed encoded-mixture estimation, larger declared search budget or fresh uncertain-boundary systems supply a new comparison.

experiments.question: Do the stored overlapping-form product distributions satisfy a published three-component identification condition?
experiments.outcome: All 36 profiles under two declared rational population conventions have fixed paired-slot ranks 3/3/3 and positive unshifted/rotated weights. The rank sum 9 meets threshold 8, identifying form weights and six slot distributions up to a common label permutation within the fixed three-component product model. Alpha 1 controls have rank one and distinct positive mixing vectors giving the same law.
experiments.challenge: The stored binary64 probabilities need an exact population convention. A first audit incorrectly required five-symbol support at zero shared mass, while cumulative rounding can give the final code tiny positive mass.
experiments.remedy: Freeze normalized-rational and continuous-uniform threshold conventions before rank tests. Use nonzero rational minors and independent elimination, retain the failed review, and correct only its support expectation. Reconstruct 345,600 pair entries and certify 288 minors.
experiments.retry_when: A changed component count, dependent-slot mechanism, fixed alternative grouping or new source-backed parameter population changes the mathematical premises.

experiments.question: Which existing observations and tools can support a restricted Indus reading, and what independent evidence is missing?
experiments.outcome: Reviewed the 101-entry baseline and four papers. All 66 Harappa tablet faces and 353 of 355 nominated numerical-class rows fall outside the principal length filter. Lothal repeated-string/contact records support a bounded physical-use test. Eight capacity rows supply no eligible independent quantity target. Object-specific count, operation or referent observations remain the key inputs for a restricted reading.
experiments.challenge: Graphic prediction, generated correspondence recovery, fitted quantities and historical interpretation have different input requirements; short source-defined records were largely absent from the main predictor's population.
experiments.remedy: Map all entries to seventeen capability families, inventory actual schemas/images/source frames, retain original semantic proposals separately, calculate descriptive compatibility and name specimen-specific acquisition and validation targets.
experiments.retry_when: A named independent quantity, referent, original source packet, corrected specimen join or historically justified reference changes the readiness of a specific test. Use the named prior audit before repeating a capability experiment.

experiments.question: Which data connections contribute original measurements, useful applications or source curation, and which publications deserve priority?
experiments.outcome: Reviewed four manuscripts and primary counterprecedents. Defensible contributions are exact measured evaluations, finite inference cases and checked source joins. Ranked empirical prediction first, focused conditional reference laws next, and a physical-source data note as another useful deliverable.
experiments.challenge: General methods and broad archaeological connections have direct predecessors; the new regional calculations continued after the review endpoint.
experiments.remedy: Use a self-contained independent brief, inspect close primary sources, check stated numbers and links, attribute predecessor observations and preserve the review endpoint separately from subsequent regional analysis.
experiments.retry_when: A new exact contribution, independently reviewed archaeological result or closer primary counterprecedent changes a particular originality or publication claim.

experiments.question: Can western and Central Asian sources join repeated marks to masses, counts, units or complete inventories?
experiments.outcome: Joined Susa SB13677/AS2615 to its museum record and reconstructed the published 25:1:2 weight proposal, requiring 0.944619% symmetric variation. Censused 69 explicitly coded Susa entries, with 57 eligible mass/mark ratios. Audited all 938 Greater Indus weight entries including 870 Dholavira objects. Located the Gonur 26-token hoard's original figure and context recovery targets.
experiments.challenge: Creation dates are missing for repeated marked groups; accession collisions, incomplete mass and mixed marks limit comparisons. Catalogue line breaks and grouping errors affected census v1. The Gonur original inventory and newer Susa chapter remain unavailable.
experiments.remedy: Retain attributed historical coefficients, calculate exact sensitivity intervals, preserve census v1 and correct it in v2, exclude unresolved collisions, audit complete catalogue coverage and name exact registrations, rooms and plate targets.
experiments.retry_when: Dated marked-weight assemblages, all-face mark photographs, a readable unit control, Gonur Fig.41 and inventory, or DHR context joins supply new source observations.

experiments.question: Which South Indian catalogue connections provide a finite stroke population and specimen targets for numerical tests?
experiments.outcome: Acquired the 2026 catalogue volumes and 48-route web snapshot. Counted 480 plain-stroke occurrences and 194 explicit stroke compounds; 142 have one stroke block and one other component. Found four literal cross-route identifier differences and independently confirmed missing stroke and base/variant discrepancies at 4.19C.
experiments.challenge: The API supplies separate context margins without joint specimen quantities or dates. Apparent full-book downloads were a brochure and a preview. Complete component naming excluded useful compounds in the initial calculation.
experiments.remedy: Preserve string identifiers and source namespaces, inspect actual PDF page counts, keep raw inputs local-only, retain the 115-form endpoint and declare a separate 194-form membership refinement, compare printed specimen tables and preserve digital discrepancies.
experiments.retry_when: An individually registered graffiti/Tamili specimen gains a readable numerical expression, measured vessel or deposit quantity, dated context, or photographic adjudication of a normalized compound.

experiments.question: Do the omitted Harappa two-code faces show real count or module variation across registered tablets?
experiments.outcome: All 66 faces on 22 tablets are retained. Twenty tablets share the same exact unordered module set; H2237 changes the C variant and H2238 changes the imported A stroke token. Five complete native-source profiles have C3-A4-D3; no count-difference pair is directly confirmed. Computed 231 object-pair comparisons and finite unresolved-count bounds.
experiments.challenge: Source readability is uneven across production groups. H2238's count and three lower-face arrangements remain unresolved. Unregistered cohort photos cannot identify H2238, and a wrong schema key omitted positions in main-v1.
experiments.remedy: Join caption registrations, preserve native counts separately from imported codes, render variant fonts, keep uncertain photo counts and physical orientation conventions, preserve main-v1 and repair displayed positions in main-v2, independently check all pairs and bounds.
experiments.retry_when: Registered raking-light, RTI or 3D views of H2238/H2230/H2234/H2237 and matched production controls resolve counts, variants or physical orientation; an independently linked referent or quantity then supports a function test.

experiments.theme: Lothal repeated-string contacts and cut zones
experiments.question: Can available labelled Lothal views resolve contact geometry and count variation within repeated-string groups?
experiments.outcome: L206 is the sole resolved G01 contact and contradicts a sole angular board-edge prediction. Four G02 visible-zone ranges are 2-4, 3-5, 3-5 and 2-3; their intersection is three. Coverage differs and complete-object totals are unavailable. Two source-informed model readings and all 21 targets are retained.
experiments.challenge: Dark halftone pictures cannot certify L193's earlier angular interpretation; unpictured members and unlabelled insets limit coverage. Selected count zones expose different fractions of surfaces.
experiments.remedy: Crop named views without pixel alterations, preserve first and second readings separately, leave topology unresolved where appropriate, avoid duplicate-view counts, compute interval intersection with scope recorded and retain missing objects in the denominator.
experiments.retry_when: Complete calibrated marked surfaces, a second resolved G01 contact junction, same-die adjudication or independent quantity observations add information absent from the current plates.

experiments.question: What original evidence connects Gonur tokens and the Altyn Depe impressed object to inventories and contexts?
experiments.outcome: Recovered original 1998, 2005 and 2008 publications. Gonur reports 26 tokens; its photograph and drawing panels each show 23 representations. Altyn Depe Plate 94.2 gives one item, three views, Excavation 5, horizon 11 and room 18, with a tentative seal-imprint caption. The original elephant-seal context is recovered.
experiments.challenge: Individual token IDs, panel correspondence, numbered hoard room and hoard date are missing. A nested book link initially returned 404.
experiments.remedy: Recover official public downloads, preserve the original caption classification, count representations in separate panels, confirm counts with a second source-informed model and resolve the book link against the domain root.
experiments.retry_when: Individual token inventories, reverse views, marked-object photographs or a deposit/date join add observations beyond the illustrated panel sample.

experiments.theme: Susa mass, mark and context source audit
experiments.question: Do original catalogues and museum images support the modern marked-weight packets?
experiments.outcome: Recovered three signed mass discrepancies, including AS 13820 changing from 2769 g to 3067 g. Two original ducks described as unmarked conflict with modern stroke counts. Recovered the four-cup image, an AS 13855 four-stroke 335 g comparison, twelfth-century BCE deposition of SB 17774 and a cross-weight locator mismatch.

experiments.retry_when: Independent SB/AS concordance, conservation/weighing history, all-face marked photographs, dated assemblages or AS13855 modern registration resolves a source disagreement.

experiments.theme: South Indian original numeral and specimen contexts
experiments.question: Can source numeral readings be joined to physical referents or registered contexts?
experiments.outcome: The original 2005 report joins a proposed 408 reading to AGM-2, depth 1.40 m, stratum 2 and drawing 2. The original Tondur account joins three reported horizontal strokes to three beds in Panchanampadi cave. Alagankulam_044 joins letters, a separate graphic and context; Alagankulam_004 supplies a registered photographed stroke specimen.

experiments.retry_when: A readable Tondur impression plus bed census, original 408 accession, exact graffiti/Tamili concordance, calibrated vessel capacity or independently documented specimen quantity becomes available.

experiments.theme: Registered Harappa and Lothal source views
experiments.question: Can better original views resolve the selected tablet counts and Lothal contact geometry?
experiments.outcome: Recovered additional labelled CISI1 Lothal panels, museum registrations and Helsinki photograph numbers, a colour L190 front image and a dated Harappa collection statement. New L190 side views leave contact topology unresolved; alternate scan plate pixels are identical.
experiments.challenge: Useful source views remain small, the front image hides the rear contact, and new registered Harappa target views remain unavailable. The alternate PDF adds no resolution.
