experiments.retry_when: Calibrated registered surfaces, original high-resolution photographs, RTI or 3D views resolve a disputed Harappa count or a second G01 continuous contact junction.

experiments.question: Does a holistic Indus dataset already exist, how does the local collection compare, and what would a measurably better public dataset require?
experiments.outcome: Established ICIT and CISI as broad predecessors, verified ICIT's 2023 counts on the original conference page, inspected three relevant Hugging Face cards via public APIs, and replayed 39 local count/missingness checks. Defined a common object register, proposed 200-object review pilot, source-specific release requirements and matched-object quality comparisons. No integrated new corpus or public release has been completed.
experiments.challenge: Historical counts, transcription records, physical objects, image witnesses and synthetic examples have different denominators. Much existing input overlaps or has unresolved rights, and ICIT's current internal coverage was not available.
experiments.remedy: Keep count bases explicit, preserve pinned discovery witnesses locally, expose source placeholders separately, carry source versions and uncertainty through the proposed schema, and require measured improvements before superiority claims.
experiments.retry_when: A current ICIT export or documented permission, new published source census, reviewed object joins, independently measured context, or newly released holistic corpus changes the coverage or feasibility comparison. Populate and review a new dataset endpoint rather than rerunning unchanged transcription benchmarks.

experiments.question: Do modified Kneser–Ney, masked recurrent/transformer models, metadata and outside-population text improve the saved Paper 001 known-slot benchmark, and do learning curves show remaining data gains?
experiments.outcome: MKN without extra: 39.7178% top-one, 4.581891 bits on 8,009 identical queries. Neural families alone do not beat MKN; ensemble with extra: 41.1662%, 4.347675 native bits. Extra text gives no measurable top-one gain; 72–94% of its common-loss gain comes from 251 outside-alphabet targets (94% for MKN, −0.2990 bits total). All four curves rise 1.21–1.71 points from 75% to 100% training.
experiments.challenge: Paper 001 component-held-out independence: 16 identical one-/two-sign texts on different objects create 144–159 linked training strings/fold, joining 192 strings and 748 queries (9.3%); no links with a three-sign threshold. Reviewer removal estimates: −8.02/−8.96/−5.88 touched-query points for first/second/MKN, implied −0.75/−0.84/−0.55 benchmark points; ranking unchanged, paired shifts at most 0.30 points. One-edit neighbours cover 509 strings (31.9%), with removal estimates −1.47/−2.32/−1.80 benchmark points. Reused masks, outcome-defined frequency ECE, post-outcome auxiliary loss and transformer epoch cap constrain interpretation.
experiments.remedy: Exact query correspondence, nested selection and full extra-face closure verified by the reviewer. Preserve numerical endpoints and frozen recipe; append dated smoothing/timing/epoch errata; use reviewer graph, neighbour and loss-decomposition evidence, position calibration and refreshed plotting metadata.
experiments.retry_when: A newly acquired source-reviewed population can test the frozen recipe without retuning; any longer-training or different neural family needs a new exploratory protocol and fresh endpoints.

experiments.theme: site and publication census of Indus inscribed evidence
experiments.question: Is all findable evidence for the Indus script indexed somewhere, and with how much archaeological and publication metadata?
experiments.outcome: Built a reproducible 89-row site and region label register from 78 literal Lipi site values plus eleven region/site leads. Counted 5,680 Lipi rows (78 site values) and 179 Mayig rows (Mohenjo-daro). Identified 17 publication records and seven site-specific excavation-report volumes at four sites, plus a primary Harappa chapter. Three reported site-count leads were retained with separate count bases; zero finds were confirmed absent from all checked indexes. An all-evidence indexed share and overall metadata-completeness rates remain unestimable without a complete published-find denominator and object-level catalogue access.
experiments.challenge: ICIT's full catalogue requires permission. The CISI publications and excavation reports overlap but do not expose a shared public object key; published counts mix seals, sealings, texts, faces, sign occurrences and images. Several recent report leads lack verified joins to corpus identifiers.
experiments.remedy: Reuse the pinned local dataset audit, count site labels by literal JSONL rows, identify primary and institutional publication records, preserve source-specific count units, record access failures, and label unverified index matches as candidates rather than omissions.
experiments.retry_when: A permissioned ICIT object export, full CISI site indexes or newly acquired excavation reports with registration/context tables permit a reviewed object-level join. Repeat counts only when a specified source version or an independent full-object list becomes available.

experiments.question: What site, publication, inscription-count, metadata, later-find, custody and digital-access evidence can be recovered for Pakistan and Afghanistan?
experiments.outcome: Revised 37 label rows / 36 site entities; minimum 3 new distinct queries per row; 375 search/inspection records and 669 source records. Final publications identified for 13 rows, 1 full final-report scan inspected. Strict dated post-CISI finds 0. M77 matched total 2596 included objects versus 4732 local faces / 3805 families / 3565 identifiers.
experiments.challenge: Incomplete later CISI access, mixed catalogue units, unresolved object provenance and missing complete excavation inventories.
experiments.remedy: Preserved 25 first-pass files, inspected primary catalogues and M77 tables, joined exact local aggregates, recorded source-specific count units and field-level failures, repaired UTF-8.
experiments.retry_when: Full later CISI pages, final excavation inventories or institutional object records permit source-page and physical-object reconciliation.

experiments.question: Which site-level inscription inventories, excavation histories and metadata can be sourced for Gujarat, Kutch and Maharashtra, retaining the requested Nuhato cross-reference?
experiments.outcome: 25 sites;130 actual queries; at least3 site-specific queries/site;496 local faces/460 families;317 CISI1 catalogue object slots across10 sites;175 Mahadevan1977 selected objects across5 sites;12 completed reports identified,6 relevant passages read. Two direct catalogue baselines with later finds plus Nuhato with report-cited baseline;13 ICIT-based published sign aggregates,1446 signs, excluded from object totals.
experiments.challenge: First pass had unsupported values and search descriptions; full final inventories and Rojdi CISI3.2 pages unavailable; count units and selection rules differ; some downloads failed or returned challenge pages.
experiments.remedy: Archive ten originals with hashes; preserve actual searches/access failures; inspect primary passages and catalogue plates; retain count disagreements and site-specific unresolved fields; UTF-8 current files.
experiments.retry_when: Full Rojdi CISI3.2, Nuhato CISI2 p.390 or unread final object inventories become available, or the local export gains registration/source crosswalks.

experiments.question: What published excavation, inscription-count and object-metadata evidence is available for the northern India batch, and how does it compare with the local export?
experiments.outcome: 25 rows, 223 executed follow-up queries, minimum five distinct queries/site, and an opened primary/substantial source at all 25. Six final-monograph sites identified; nine sites with reported post-1987 inscribed finds, including three previously catalogued in CISI 1. Nine CISI 1 sections contain 176 catalogue objects; local totals are 290 faces, 271 families, 232 distinct CISI IDs. Counts keep units, dates and eligibility separate.
experiments.challenge: Disk-full interruption; conflicting coordinates and count bases; 22 failed downloads; inaccessible later CISI and final inventories; incomplete registration joins and current custody.
experiments.remedy: Audited recovered files, preserved ten first-pass files, removed 253209317 bytes of temporary renders, rebuilt UTF-8 outputs, inspected primary pages and retained exact search/failure records. Unresolved fields link to their searches and inspected sources.
experiments.retry_when: When CISI 3.2 Kalibangan pages, Farmana/Tarkhanewala final inventories, Mahadevan Appendix V or ICIT site-count pages become accessible; when new object-specific season, registration or custody records permit reconciliation.

experiments.theme: Foreign-find site census and corpus provenance
experiments.question: Which published Indus-related objects occur at the requested foreign sites, and what evidence and local coverage can be established?
experiments.outcome: 36 rows cover 23 named sites, all 27 local regional labels and Babylon. Local totals are 42 faces and 42 object-family labels. Fourteen final-report bibliographies and nine coordinate witnesses were identified. Selected mixed-class object minima sum to 36 across 22 rows; complete coverage fractions remain undefined. Four later inscription-related reports were recorded, with zero matched post-CISI cutoffs. The build and independent reference/CSV/hash checks pass.
experiments.challenge: Mixed glyptic and other-script catalogue sequences, uncertain signs, production/findspot labels, blocked downloads and incomplete object joins prevent a complete site inventory. Several geography, campaign, custody and main-publication metadata fields remain unresolved after searches.
experiments.remedy: Preserved local figures and counting units; added CISI 3.3 (2022) through a dated protocol amendment; recovered original Nippur and Tell Asmar reports through current ISAC S3 routes; retained every query, snippet and failed acquisition locally; provided source-linked rows and deterministic checks.
experiments.retry_when: Actual CISI plates, Kjaerum's catalogue, inaccessible final reports, Mahadevan/ICIT site subtotals or specimen photographs become available for reviewed object joins; dedicated geographic authorities can resolve remaining locations.

experiments.question: Do public museum catalogues, corpora and image archives index findable evidence for the Indus script, and which metadata fields can be joined?
experiments.outcome: Focused pass: 114 inspected inscription-confirmed original records across New Delhi 76, Kolkata 18, British Museum 6 cached witnesses, Penn 5, Louvre 4 and Met website 5; these are bounded minima. Portal seven-term union has 4007 record IDs and 158 candidate pages, yielding 94 unique originals and 10 plaster copies. Penn Indus Script filter has 34 records: 5 originals and 29 plaster impressions. 61/114 originals (53.51%) join to 61 corpus families / 67 faces; 80 carry usable identifier keys and 61/80 (76.25%) match. Audit methods: 13 exact, 6 normalized, 36 CISI published concordance, 5 shared field/plate, 1 Marshall composite. Thirty confirmed pairs selected deterministically; all 61 retained. HR 5635345 resolved via Marshall 1931 II p. 404, row 345 = HR 5635. Missing sampled metadata: bibliography 101/114, dimensions 25/114. One site, four material, five comparable dimension and nine single-face sign-count differences flagged.
experiments.challenge: British Museum and MFA requests HTTP 403; Louvre search 429 though object JSON works; NMMA timeouts; National Museum of Pakistan SSL transfer failure and no object-level inventory located. Complete institutional inscription totals remain unmeasured. Corpus identifiers include concatenated publication references and an identifier collision at DKI838; 53 sampled originals remain unjoined. Museum and corpus terminology, dimension coverage and sign segmentation differ.
experiments.remedy: Use portal internal JSON route with museumId=all, complete pagination and accession deduplication; use Met website instead of failed API; use explicit CISI museum/excavation concordances and Penn published plate references. Preserve all failed routes, source values and uncertain joins in raw storage. Record image/data rights separately; keep unresolved-rights payloads local. Keep previous pass in history/2026-10-07-depth-pass.
experiments.retry_when: Independent reviewer repeats 30 confirmed pairs and checks the full 61-row audit; functioning BM/MFA/NMMA inventories or Pakistan object-level records permit wider inscription counts; published concordances resolve the remaining 53 unjoined sampled records.

experiments.question: Is all discoverable Indus evidence indexed with its available metadata, and what would a complete index require?
experiments.outcome: Reviewed v6 uses post-trim inputs. 123 rows join to 115 site/provenance entities; 5,652 of 5,680 local faces fall in their label frame. Across 19 CISI 1 ranges, 327 of 493 identifiers match and 166 are absent: 75 in pottery/graffiti sections and 91 in other sections. Complete Pakistan multi-run parsing gives 910/1,040 matching keys; north IM77 total is corrected to 117. Museum confirmed lower bound is 68/114, with 46 unresolved. Eight catalogue sections lack rows. Worldwide object recall remains unknown.
experiments.challenge: Post-endpoint coordinator title edits made earlier pins stale; inherited IM77 error and first-run-only parsing required source-backed corrections. Mixed classes, provisional physical identities and inaccessible current inventories prevent a global denominator.
experiments.remedy: Preserve prior endpoints; record post-trim hashes, parse all runs with the H356/H354 corrigendum, check seven additional museum joins, distinguish structural field absences and pass 53 proposed batch corrections without changing batch rows.
experiments.retry_when: Independent review identifies a correction, or current ICIT/full CISI/holding inventories, new registration concordances or original context/rights records become available. Recompute only in a new dated endpoint with the changed input or method recorded.

experiments.question: Which project results outside script decipherment have field-specific publication potential, and what is the smallest credible next deliverable for each?
experiments.outcome: Corrected the first pass after Sonnet review. Inventory now contains 26 records, with 25 assessed candidates and one held evidence-census pointer without results. All 112 registry IDs have one primary checklist home across 24 records, with original statuses and secondary cross-links retained. Added CISI scan duplication, cross-catalogue joins and the completed October 2 dataset landscape; incorporated capacity, Susa reconstruction and Harappa module audits. Revised priority order, subject precedent checks, source provenance and venue/form conditions are in inventory.json and REPORT.md.
experiments.challenge: The registry mixes primary endpoints, sensitivities, source audits, proposals, and failed paths. Grouping them risks hiding status differences or overstating novelty; many source assets also have unresolved redistribution rights.
experiments.remedy: Preserve first-pass files and the dated amendment, remove unfinished sibling-package results, bind corrected claims to saved fields, repair registry homes and source records, keep simulations and post-outcome work explicit, and name only article-form matches supported by opened venue pages. Package checks validate bookkeeping and saved fields; source identities, expert readings, exact novelty and deposit rights remain candidate-specific gaps.
experiments.retry_when: A new source review, venue/editor response, rights determination, independent reproduction, or a materially broader precedent search changes a candidate's readiness or ranking.

experiments.theme: chronological/regional graphic variation; matched external inscriptions; caption-led media/inventory; excavation-composition review response
experiments.question: Does Harappa sign usage change across recorded HARP periods after object-type and excavation-frame controls; do sampled regions differ; and do exact type/length-matched external texts differ? Caption-led amendments test graphic human candidates, media diversity and early inventory. The second amendment reruns references at larger budgets and checks label-source/mound composition.
experiments.outcome: Primary endpoint: Frozen evaluation; later amendments: Exploratory; arithmetic and replay checks: Verified computation. On 5680 faces, full 3B–3C equal-type JS=.190483 bits, seed-21 null=.157180 and excess=.033303, Holm=.0392/.0358 (seeds 21/22); closure=.06500/.06265 on its smaller population. Period-labelled JS=.219445, null=.176564, excess=.042881, Holm=.0342/.0310. Mound-E JS=.244466, null=.206696, excess=.037770, Holm=.06545/.06555. No usable JS magnitude interval is supplied. Period 2–3C pottery Holm=.06075/.06305. Sign 034 has BH=.0432/.0444; all other time signs and all 314 regional signs fail .05. Four of six regional physical tests and two closure tests pass in both seeds. Length increase .723952 slots falls to .162414 for period-labelled and .115848 for Mound-E frames, with restricted intervals spanning zero. External matching retains 7/42 objects, type-model surprisal excess=.650896 [-.379864,1.857194], pooled excess=-.086317, score-family Holm=1 in both seeds. Raw external 090/091 counts are 7/149 and 5/149 versus core 184/17792 and 22/17792, entirely on circular seals; supported matches contain neither target, enrichment Holm=1. Full/period-labelled/Mound-E rarefied media richness increases 4.598459/3.742102/4.361847; all richness and Shannon Holm values below .05 in both seeds. Early 2/3A has 18 signs and 37 known tokens in 31 families; exact type/length support retains 27 early/12 later pottery families, expected-inventory difference=.120190, Holm=.5046/.5077. Every frequency threshold decision agrees across seeds. Existing endpoints unchanged.
experiments.challenge: Excavation sources differ: 9/201 3B versus 405/574 3C stratum labels; 180/201 3B from Mound E versus 413/574 3C from F. Only 392/405 3C stratum faces have parseable earlier-range catalogue numbers; 13 are missing. Region is fixed by site; copying reduces supported populations. Sparse JS bootstrap intervals are unusable; early inventory union bootstraps are shifted. Circular seals lack exact comparators and matched external objects are mostly standard types, including Baluchistan/Makran context. Earliest support is small pottery, rather than a representative seal repertoire. The 3C bin cannot locate a 2100 BCE breakpoint. 96 site/type and 25 region/type singleton cells disclose source-derived data in immutable private outputs. Full underlying Parpola 1983/1986/1994 and Kenoyer–Meadow 2008 chapters, exact lecture glyphs, independent 091 mapping and archaeological row identities remain unchecked. Fuls excerpt attribution is withdrawn; direct retry returned 403.
experiments.remedy: Keep complete physical aliases and transitive text components before selection; permute exact-type/multiplicity blocks and report each reference population. Use seeds 21/22 with 19999 time and 9999 other allocations, Holm/BH correction, Monte Carlo errors and null mean/excess. Restrict separately to period-labelled and Mound-E families and report raw/adjusted length and media effects. Candidates and alternatives were specified before the matched-frequency computation, with earlier broad counts available; timing is evidenced by file times only. Preserve interval allocation assumptions, model training-size sensitivities and unsupported circular classes.
